annotations.target_phrase: Maelcum, pilot of the Marcus Garvey, dreadlocks floating in zero-g
annotations.annotation_text: Maelcum serves as the orbital tug pilot whose space vessel, the Marcus Garvey (named after the Pan-Africanist leader), bridges Rastafarian liberation theology with hard vacuum orbital mechanics.
sources: Brians, Paul. Study Guide for William Gibson: Neuromancer (1984). WSU.
Murphy, Graham J. William Gibson's Neuromancer: A Critical Companion. Palgrave, 2024.

annotations.target_phrase: Aerol and the Zion elders, reading scripture and consulting the dub console
annotations.annotation_text: The Zion elders interpret technological telemetry through prophetic Rastafarian scripture. They view Case's mission not as a corporate theft but as an assault on Babylon, sanctifying their participation in the heist.
sources: Brians, Paul. Study Guide for William Gibson: Neuromancer (1984). WSU.
